nodes.summary: For all words $p$ and $t$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, the list of offsets returned by the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$ equals the list returned by the naive matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$, entry by entry and in the same order. Only the returned lists are compared, not the costs.
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore agrees with the naive matcher

nodes.summary: For every text $t$ of length $n$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, the Boyer–Moore matcher with the empty pattern and text $t$ returns the list $0, 1, \dots, n$ of all offsets from $0$ to $n$ in increasing order, at cost $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore with the empty pattern

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$. If $t$ is strictly shorter than $p$, then the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$ returns the empty list at cost $0$: no preprocessing or search events are charged.
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore with a pattern longer than the text

nodes.summary: For all words $p$ and $t$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, the list of offsets returned by the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$ is strictly increasing: each entry is smaller than every entry after it.
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore returns offsets in strictly increasing order

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ of lengths $m$ and $n$. The cost of the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$ is at most $n + 1$ if $m = 0$, at most $0$ if $n < m$, and at most $\sigma + n + 11m - 6 + (m + 4)(n - m + 1)$ if $1 \le m \le n$.
nodes.title: Worst-case cost of Boyer–Moore matching

nodes.summary: Exact Boyer–Moore cost when the pattern repeats one letter and ends in another, which alone makes up the text. Let $a \ne b$ be letters of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ and let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $2 \le m \le n$. Write $a^{m-1}b$ for the word of $m - 1$ copies of $a$ followed by one $b$, and $b^n$ for the word of $n$ copies of $b$. The cost of the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern…
nodes.title: Exact Boyer–Moore cost when the pattern repeats one letter and ends in another, which alone makes up the text

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a letter of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $0 < m \le n$, and write $x^k$ for the word of $k$ copies of $x$. The cost of the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $x^m$ and text $x^n$ equals $m + n + P + (m + 4)(n - m + 1)$, where $P$ is the cost of the Boyer–Moore preprocessing of the pattern $x^m$.
nodes.title: Exact Boyer–Moore cost when pattern and text repeat the same letter

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ and $t = t_0 \cdots t_{n-1}$ be words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$. The matcher returns a list of offsets together with a cost. If $m = 0$ it returns $0, 1, \dots, n$ at cost $n + 1$, and if $n < m$ it returns the empty list at cost $0$. Otherwise it charges $m + n$ for converting $p$ and $t$ to arrays, computes the bad-character table $B$ and the strong good-suffix…
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore matcher for all occurrences

nodes.summary: For all words $p$ and $t$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ and every natural number $k$, the offset $k$ belongs to the list returned by the Boyer–Moore matcher with pattern $p$ and text $t$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $t$ at offset $k$, that is, $k \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the word obtained from $t$ by deleting its first $k$ letters. In particular, overlapping occurrences are all returned.
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore returns exactly the occurrences

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ and let $B$ be the bad-character table computed by the Boyer–Moore preprocessing of $p$. For every symbol $c$, either $B_c = m$ and $p_k \ne c$ for every $k$ with $k + 1 < m$, or there is $j$ with $j + 1 < m$ and $p_j = c$ such that $B_c = m - 1 - j$ and every $k$ with $k + 1 < m$ and $p_k = c$ satisfies $k \le j$.
nodes.title: Bad-character table of Boyer–Moore preprocessing

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a nonempty pattern over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ and let $G$ be the good-suffix table computed by the Boyer–Moore preprocessing of $p$. Then $1 \le G_0 \le m$, $p_{t - G_0} = p_t$ for every $t < m$ with $G_0 \le t$, and $G_0 \le e$ for every positive integer $e$ such that $p_{t - e} = p_t$ for every $t < m$ with $e \le t$. That is, $G_0$ is the least positive period of…
nodes.title: The full-match shift is the least period of the pattern

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, let $G$ be the good-suffix table computed by the Boyer–Moore preprocessing of $p$, and let $i < m$. Call a positive integer $e$ an admissible shift at $i$ if $p_{t - e} = p_t$ for every $t < m$ with $i < t$ and $e \le t$, and $p_{i - e} \ne p_i$ whenever $e \le i$. Then $1 \le G_i \le m$ and $G_i$ is the least admissible shift…
nodes.title: Good-suffix table of Boyer–Moore preprocessing

nodes.summary: For a pattern of length $m$ over an alphabet of size $\sigma$, the event cost of the Boyer–Moore preprocessing is at most $\sigma$ when $m = 0$ and at most $\sigma + 10m - 6$ when $m \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Cost of Boyer–Moore preprocessing

nodes.summary: Given a pattern $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$, this computes a bad-character table $B$ of length $\sigma$ and a strong good-suffix table $G$ of length $m$. The table $B$ starts with every entry equal to $m$, and then for $k = 0, 1, \dots, m - 2$ in turn the entry $B_{p_k}$ is set to $m - 1 - k$. For $G$, let $s_i$ be the length of the longest common suffix of $p_0 \cdots p_i$…
nodes.title: Boyer–Moore preprocessing

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
